key_insight: Selective Chain-of-Thought (Selective CoT) first predicts whether a medical question needs step-by-step reasoning and generates a rationale only when required, cutting unnecessary reasoning without hurting answer accuracy.
problem_solved: Reduces wasted compute, latency, and token cost from generating chain-of-thought for straightforward MedQA items by selectively invoking reasoning only for questions that truly need it.
method: Inference-time binary predictor classifies each question as ‘needs reasoning’ vs ‘direct answer’.
Conditional CoT: generate chain-of-thought rationale only when the predictor signals reasoning is required; otherwise return a concise answer.
Empirical evaluation on two open LLMs (Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen-2.5-7B) across four biomedical benchmarks (HeadQA, MedQA-USMLE, MedMCQA, …) to measure accuracy vs efficiency trade-offs.
impact: Enables faster, cheaper, and scalable MedQA deployments by avoiding unnecessary reasoning while preserving diagnostic-quality answers — useful for production LLM pipelines in healthcare and resource-constrained settings.

paper_title: To Reason or Not to: Selective Chain-of-Thought in Medical Question Answering
paper_authors: Zaifu Zhan, Min Zeng, Shuang Zhou, Yiran Song, Xiaoyi Chen
